outcome: C-reactive protein (CRP) levels at 1, 12, and 36 hours
cohort: The study included term infants born after prolonged rupture of membranes lasting 24 hours or more, without evidence of sepsis.
finding: Median C-reactive protein (CRP) levels were low in term infants without sepsis born after prolonged rupture of membranes, but individual outliers showed CRP levels exceeding 60, 80, and 90 mg/L at 1, 12, and 36 hours respectively.
mod_finding: There was no difference in C-reactive protein levels between infants born via C-section versus vaginal delivery.
